Industrial Digitalization in the MENA Region

Following a surge in investment volume in 2025, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) technology ecosystem is transitioning in 2026 to a phase of industrial maturity, where technology—driven by autonomous systems and physical digitalization—dominates the economy. Infrastructure investments, led particularly by Saudi Arabia and the UAE, are transforming the region’s technology capacity into a global-scale production and R&D hub.

Key Technological Focus Areas in 2026

The key technology trends accelerating the region’s digital transformation are based on the evolution of artificial intelligence from text-generating systems to autonomous decision-making mechanisms, as well as blockchain-based asset management.

  • Agentic AI: AI models are evolving into corporate partners capable of making autonomous decisions. The integration of task-oriented AI agents into enterprise applications is rapidly increasing, significantly reducing manual workloads.
  • Physical AI and Robotics: Digital intelligence is merging with industrial production lines and humanoid robot technologies, moving from pilot phases to commercial-scale deployment. The market share of domestically produced industrial robots is expanding.
  • Ambient Intelligence and IoT: Thanks to standardized protocols for the Internet of Things (such as Matter) and 5G infrastructure, sensor data and artificial intelligence are converging to establish preventive systems in sectors such as energy and healthcare.
  • Real-World Assets (RWA) and Tokenization: Financial technologies are moving beyond traditional payment infrastructures toward deeper structures such as open finance APIs and the tokenization of real estate and hardware investments via blockchain (ARVA).

Smart City Ecosystems and Infrastructure

Cognitive city projects like NEOM—one of the region’s largest-scale technology test beds—are bringing to life urban designs that run on 100% renewable energy and operate through AI’s autonomous decisions, from healthcare management to logistics. Investments in manufacturing facilities, server infrastructure, and robotic research laboratories—simulated using digital twin technologies—are accelerating the transformation of theoretical projects into physical reality.
